newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran manager sees oil traders part of "family".
newsitem.headline: Iran manager sees oil traders part of "family".

text.p: A senior Iranian oil official on Thursday embraced foreign oil traders as members of the same "international family of the oil market."
Deputy Oil Minister Hojatollah Ghanimifard, who is in charge of Iran's crude exports at the National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC), said "honest" traders had a rightful role in play in the oil business.
Traders were already buyers of Iranian crude on the spot market and also under regular term contracts, he said.
State-owned NIOC has had testy relationships with some foreign trading firms which it felt were manipulating prices of Iranian crude or not fully honouring contract conditions.
NIOC's close and lucrative ties with U.S. oil firms and traders were dashed in 1995 when President Bill Clinton imposed sanctions against the Islamic republic.
Iran is the world's third largest oil exporter after Saudi Arabia and Norway. Annual petrodollar earnings run at $18 billion.
